title: General discussion on RFC-0035 (FIPS) and RFC-0036 (Phase 4 pilot)
author: pete-gov
body:
Hey all - as a reminder, FedRAMP can't answer questions or generally participate directly in RFC threads to avoid influencing public comment. Sometimes this creates confusion because folks just want to talk about details of something proposed in an RFC to understand it better or learn more about it, so we create these side-threads at times for RFCs.

The two open RFCs in question are:

- #179 
- #180 

Please feel free to use this thread to discuss, ask questions, etc. - but don't forget to add public comment with feedback either way!

comments.author: StevenCh99
comments.body:
With regards to: FRC-CLD-CTP:
"Providers seeking a FedRAMP 20x Class D Certification SHOULD limit the likely handling of federal customer data within the cloud service offering to third-party information resources that are included in a FedRAMP Class B, Class C, Class D, or Class G Certified offering."

What is a Class G Certified offering? I do not believe I have seen or heard references to that previously.

Thank you!

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body: That is a tiny little spoiler hiding in there. :) In RFC-0032, we proposed a separate process for FedRAMP Certification of cloud service offerings that were provided by federal agencies - if approved by the FR Board later this month, that will be Class G to differentiate it from commercial classes.

comments.author: HazemEld
comments.body: The _Notes_ in the rules are undefeated. My favorite is the one in CMU-CSO-TSC: "Adding a non-validated algorithm while a CMVP-validated module still protects federal customer data, such as hybrid implementation, is not such a change." Allows a CSP to add a PQC-approved algo. as an option to the algo that was validated as part of the module without going through a transformative.

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body: Hmmm, just to clarify, that note means you can use a CMVP-validated module to protect information _and then wrap it in a PQC resistant algo that isn't CMVP-validated_ (or vice versa) and that's likely not a transformative change (and it's good security). This hybrid implementation can be a bit expensive but it's the most effective way to dot the i's and cross the t's for any customers that are quite picky about sticking with CMVP-validated modules.

replies.author: HazemEld
replies.body: Yup, that's exactly what my interpretation of these notes were. You're clarification is a lot more clear than my reaction but we're on the same page here. Thanks you!

comments.author: kcarr91
comments.body:
Just wanted to make sure im understanding something correctly in [RFC-0036 FedRAMP 20x Class D Cloud-Hosted Pilot Requirements](https://github.com/FedRAMP/community/discussions/180)

This rule **_FRC-CLD-PCD Progressive Certification to Class D_** would apply to Class D 20x generally post pilot and not just the pilot correct?

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body: Yes, that's right, intent is to across the board require a 20x Class C assessment before moving up to 20x Class D so that FR is not having to do a full 20x Class D from scratch for anyone. As a reminder, folks with current Rev5 Class D would still retain their Rev5 Class D during that transition.

comments.author: 20xcompliance
comments.body:
**Does `FRC-CLD-PCD` apply to new Rev5 Class D Agency Certifications?**

We want to confirm our reading of `FRC-CLD-PCD` (RFC-0036). The rule applies to providers "seeking a FedRAMP 20x Class D Certification." We read it as **not** requiring a provider on the **Rev5 / Agency / Class D** Certification Profile (an agency-sponsored Rev5 Class D application filed before the June 11, 2027 cutoff for new Rev5 applications) to first hold a 20x Class C Certification for 6 months.

We also read the note that "transitions from Rev5 Class D will still be expected to move through 20x Class C first" as applying only to a later move from Rev5 Class D to 20x Class D, not to obtaining the Rev5 Class D certification.

Is that correct? Thank you.

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body:
> Is that correct? Thank you.

The entirety of RFC-0036 is for FedRAMP 20x and would not apply to FedRAMP Rev5.

comments.author: TM-Microsoft
comments.body:
Hi FedRAMP Team,

CMU-CSO-TSC (Transformative Significant Changes of Modules): Could you clarify what counts as a "change" under this rule? In particular, does it cover bug fixes and security patches, which are our most common changes? Or does it apply only to changes in the algorithms a module uses?

Thanks

replies.author: pete-gov
replies.body:
> : Could you clarify what counts as a "change" under this rule? In particular, does it cover bug fixes and security patches, which are our most common changes? Or does it apply only to changes in the algorithms a module uses?

It's intended to apply to replacing a CMVP-validated module with one that isn't (hence "**from** CMVP-validated modules **to** non-CMVP-validated modules"), so you're taking something that used to be protected with a FIPS 140-3 algo and replacing it with protection that according to NIST is no better than plain text. This would already be a significant change under the rules.

Remember that we defined "CMVP-validated modules" earlier as including upstream versions of the same module, so replacing it with upstream versions (patching) isn't replacing it with non-CMVP-validated modules.

Examples:

- MegaCrypto-3.1 with the AES-Mega9 is CMVP-validated. You patch to MegaCrypto-3.2 which has an updated version of AES-Mega9 - this proposed rule wouldn't apply and it's a routine recurring change.

- You decide MegaCrypto-3.1's version of AES-Mega9 is too slow and want to switch to ShinyCrypto-1.0 AES-ShinyShiny... but ShinyCrypto has never been CMVP-validated. This would trigger the rule and require a transformative change, because you're replacing the protection provided by a CMVP-validated module to the protection provided by a non-CMVP-validated module.
